raw_text:
The objective is to explain differences in workplace productivity variables in areas that use the same manufacturing processes and technology. This focus in encouraged by the approach to assessment that has been used to date. Both first- and second-level supervisors, and employees, evaluate whether work is complete and if it is correct. Along with this, each job has an attributed percentage of one's time.
Methodological framing
Use a Bayesian methodological approach.
Assumptions or assumptions

Frustration tolerance. The level of this may be low at times when the luxuries of grey, or perceived, asymmetric information transfer are reduced. Also, there will be time pressure to compensate for low pay by shortening the time when the overall job requires communication, rather than focussing on productivity.
Shyness with expansive openness. Even small differences in human relationships, length of time at work, past experience and so on may be reflected in people’s sense of social connection, which in turn may influence the strength of the hierarchical separation. This may be complicated however by individual workers having the same educational training.
Act of diffusion. Contagion spreads when tasks are in a temporary state of being all at a standstill, such as tasks being turned off for maintenance.
Gift exchange. The range of different standards in socio-economic background influences individual behaviour.
Being in debt undermines performance. Job frustration indicators include menstrual hygiene, digestive difficulties, envy of others, sensitivity to texture, skin diseases, indifferent service, heated temper, sleepiness, 'bad colds' and unproductiveness.
Reliability. The asymmetric flow of information due to shyness and expansiveness may influence reliability, despite the asymmetric flow of information/influence already being present from the start. Specialists do not judge overall productivity, only individual ones.
Conformance considerations. Eligibility to access benefits may increase the motivation to increase performance. In turn, this may lead to reluctance by supervisors to take firm steps to address issues such as shyness or expansiveness where it may jeopardise this.
Demand characteristics. As well as the effects of the stimuli already described surface in the workplace, workplace cultures can also arise through field experimentation accidentally having broad reliance, as people strive to gain a competitive advantage.
